redFlags.message: Chest pain with shortness of breath can signal a heart or lung emergency. Seek emergency care now.
Chest pain with an irregular heartbeat needs urgent medical assessment.
Chest pain with heavy sweating can signal a heart attack. Call emergency services.
High fever with bleeding may indicate severe dengue. Go to a hospital today.
Severe headache with vision change needs urgent evaluation.
Yellow skin with persistent vomiting needs urgent medical review.
Severe breathing difficulty — seek emergency care.
Slurred speech can signal a stroke. Call emergency services now.
Weakness on one side of the body can signal a stroke. Call emergency services now.
Unconsciousness is an emergency. Call emergency services now.
Confusion or drowsiness needs urgent medical attention.
Coughing up blood needs urgent medical evaluation.
Bleeding from the stomach is an emergency. Go to hospital now.
Blood in the stool needs prompt medical evaluation.
Signs of acute liver failure are an emergency. Go to hospital now.
High fever with a stiff neck can signal meningitis. Seek emergency care.

diseases.name: Fungal Infection
diseases.description: A skin, nail or scalp infection caused by fungi, often itchy with a ring-shaped or scaly patch.
treatment: Keep the area clean and completely dry
Use an antifungal cream for 2–4 weeks, even after it looks better
Oral antifungals for extensive, nail or scalp infections (doctor)
medications: Clotrimazole or terbinafine cream
Oral fluconazole or terbinafine: prescription only
diet: Keep blood sugar controlled if you are diabetic
diseases.seeDoctor: Spreading rash, no improvement after 2 weeks, or you are diabetic or have weak immunity.

diseases.name: Allergy
diseases.description: An over-reaction of the immune system to a harmless trigger such as pollen, dust, food or medicine.
treatment: Identify and avoid your trigger
Cool compress or calamine for itchy skin; saline rinse for the nose
People with severe allergies should carry an adrenaline auto-injector
medications: Non-drowsy antihistamines (cetirizine, loratadine)
Mild hydrocortisone cream for skin rash (short term)
diet: Avoid trigger foods; read food labels
diseases.seeDoctor: Swelling of face, lips or throat, wheezing or faintness is an emergency (anaphylaxis).

diseases.name: GERD (Acid Reflux)
diseases.description: Stomach acid flowing back into the food pipe, causing heartburn and sour taste.
treatment: Eat smaller meals; do not lie down for 3 hours after eating
Raise the head of the bed; lose weight if overweight
Short course of acid-reducing medicine
medications: Antacids, famotidine or a proton-pump inhibitor such as omeprazole (short course; ask a doctor)
tests: Endoscopy if there are warning signs
precautions: Stop smoking; limit alcohol and caffeine
Avoid fatty and very spicy trigger foods
diseases.seeDoctor: Trouble swallowing, weight loss, vomiting blood, black stools, or chest pain (which can be the heart).

diseases.name: Chronic Cholestasis
diseases.description: Reduced flow of bile from the liver, causing itching, jaundice and dark urine.
treatment: Find and treat the cause (gallstones, medicines, liver disease)
Specialist medicines to improve bile flow and relieve itching
Supplement fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K as advised
medications: Ursodeoxycholic acid and itch-relief medicines: prescription only
precautions: Review all medicines with your doctor
Stay up to date on hepatitis vaccines
diseases.seeDoctor: Jaundice, severe itching, dark urine with pale stools, or fever with abdominal pain.

diseases.name: Drug Reaction
diseases.description: An unwanted reaction to a medicine, from mild rash to life-threatening allergy.
treatment: Contact a doctor before stopping a prescribed drug; seek emergency care if severe
Antihistamines or steroids as advised by a doctor
Record the drug and tell every doctor and pharmacist
medications: Antihistamines or corticosteroids: doctor-directed
Adrenaline for anaphylaxis
precautions: Carry a list of drugs you react to
diseases.seeDoctor: Facial swelling, trouble breathing, blistering or peeling skin, mouth sores, or fever with rash: emergency.

diseases.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
diseases.description: Sores in the lining of the stomach or upper intestine, often from H. pylori infection or painkillers.
treatment: Acid-suppressing medicine for 4–8 weeks
Antibiotic combination if H. pylori is found
Stop anti-inflammatory painkillers, smoking and alcohol
medications: Proton-pump inhibitors and antibiotics: prescription only
Antacids for short-term relief
tests: H. pylori breath or stool test
precautions: Avoid long-term use of anti-inflammatory painkillers
diet: Avoid foods that trigger your pain
diseases.seeDoctor: Black or bloody stools, vomiting blood, or sudden severe abdominal pain: emergency.

diseases.name: HIV / AIDS
diseases.description: A virus that weakens the immune system. With modern treatment people can live long, healthy lives.
treatment: Confirm with an HIV test
Start antiretroviral therapy (ART) under a specialist; it is taken lifelong
Regular viral-load and CD4 monitoring; prevent and treat other infections
medications: Antiretroviral combinations: prescription only
Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) works only if started within 72 hours of exposure
precautions: Test partners; PrEP is available for people at high risk
diseases.seeDoctor: Test as soon as possible after any possible exposure, or with unexplained weight loss, long-lasting fever or diarrhea.

diseases.name: Diabetes
diseases.description: A long-term condition in which the body cannot use insulin properly, raising blood sugar.
treatment: Confirm with fasting glucose / HbA1c tests
Lifestyle changes and regular exercise
Ongoing monitoring and foot/eye checks
medications: Metformin and other glucose-lowering drugs, or insulin — prescription only
diseases.seeDoctor: Confusion, fruity breath, or vomiting with high sugar needs emergency care.

diseases.name: Gastroenteritis (Stomach Flu / Food Poisoning)
diseases.description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines from viruses, bacteria or contaminated food.
treatment: Sip oral rehydration solution frequently
Rest the stomach, then reintroduce bland food
Wash hands thoroughly
medications: ORS is the key treatment
Antiemetic or zinc (children) on medical advice
Avoid anti-diarrhea drugs if there is blood or high fever
diet: Avoid dairy (other than curd), spicy and oily food
diseases.seeDoctor: Blood in stool, signs of dehydration (dry mouth, very little urine), or symptoms beyond 2–3 days.
tests: Stool examination and culture if severe

diseases.name: Asthma
diseases.description: A chronic condition where the airways narrow and swell, causing wheeze and breathlessness.
treatment: Use a reliever inhaler at the first sign of symptoms
Identify and avoid triggers
Follow a written asthma action plan
medications: Reliever inhaler (salbutamol)
Preventer (inhaled corticosteroid) as prescribed
diet: Balanced diet with fruit and vegetables
Avoid foods that trigger your symptoms
diseases.seeDoctor: Reliever not helping, difficulty speaking, or blue lips — call emergency services.

diseases.name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
diseases.description: Persistently high blood pressure that quietly strains the heart and blood vessels.
treatment: Confirm with repeated BP readings
Lifestyle changes: salt reduction, exercise, weight control
Regular follow-up with a doctor
medications: Antihypertensives (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, calcium channel blockers, etc.) — prescription only
diet: DASH-style diet: fruit, vegetables, whole grains
diseases.seeDoctor: Readings above 180/120 with headache, chest pain or vision change need emergency care.
tests: Kidney function, lipid profile, blood sugar

diseases.name: Migraine
diseases.description: Recurring, often one-sided throbbing headaches that may come with nausea and sensitivity to light.
treatment: Rest in a quiet, dark room
Cold compress on the forehead
Track triggers with a headache diary
medications: Pain relievers (paracetamol, ibuprofen) early in an attack
Triptans or preventive medicines if prescribed
diet: Avoid known triggers (aged cheese, processed meats, alcohol)
diseases.seeDoctor: Sudden "worst headache of your life", headache with weakness, confusion or fever and stiff neck — emergency.
tests: MRI/CT only if red-flag features are present

diseases.name: Cervical Spondylosis
diseases.description: Age-related wear of the neck bones and discs causing neck pain and stiffness, sometimes with arm symptoms.
treatment: Physiotherapy and neck-strengthening exercises
Correct posture; heat packs for stiffness
Soft collar only for short periods and only if advised
medications: Paracetamol or short-term anti-inflammatory tablets
Muscle relaxants: prescription only
tests: MRI if there is numbness or weakness
precautions: Set your screen at eye level
Avoid heavy lifting on the neck and shoulders
diet: Calcium and vitamin D rich foods
diseases.seeDoctor: Arm or hand weakness, numbness, bladder or bowel changes, or trouble walking need urgent review.

diseases.name: Stroke (Brain Hemorrhage / Paralysis)
diseases.description: Blocked or burst blood vessel in the brain. This is a medical emergency where every minute matters.
treatment: Call your emergency number immediately and note the time symptoms began
Do not give food, drink or medicine
Hospital: urgent brain scan, clot-dissolving drug or clot removal, or bleeding control
Rehabilitation afterwards
medications: Treatment depends on the brain scan and is given only in hospital; never self-treat
tests: Urgent CT or MRI of the brain
precautions: Control blood pressure, diabetes and cholesterol
diseases.seeDoctor: EMERGENCY: face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty or a sudden severe headache. Call emergency services now.

diseases.name: Jaundice
diseases.description: Yellowing of the skin and eyes from excess bilirubin; it is a sign of an underlying problem, not a disease by itself.
treatment: Find the cause (liver, bile ducts, blood)
Rest, fluids and no alcohol
Treatment depends on the cause; newborns may need phototherapy
medications: Avoid self-medicating or unproven herbal "jaundice cures"; they can harm the liver
diseases.seeDoctor: Always see a doctor. Go to hospital for confusion, vomiting blood or severe abdominal pain.

diseases.name: Malaria
diseases.description: A parasitic infection spread by Anopheles mosquitoes, marked by cyclic fever with chills and sweats.
treatment: Confirm with a blood smear or rapid test
Complete the full antimalarial course prescribed
Hospital care for severe cases
medications: Antimalarials (e.g. artemisinin-based) — prescription only
diseases.seeDoctor: Any fever after being in a malaria-prone area needs testing within 24 hours.

diseases.name: Chickenpox
diseases.description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy blistering rash and fever.
treatment: Rest and fluids; calamine lotion and cool baths for itch
Keep nails short to prevent infection
Stay home until all blisters have crusted over
Antivirals for high-risk people when a doctor advises
medications: Paracetamol for fever. Do NOT give aspirin to children
Antihistamines for itching
precautions: Avoid contact with pregnant women, newborns and immunocompromised people
diet: Soft, bland foods if the mouth has sores
diseases.seeDoctor: You are pregnant, have a newborn or weak immunity, or have trouble breathing, infected blisters or fever beyond 4 days.

diseases.name: Dengue Fever
diseases.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing high fever, severe body pain and a drop in platelets.
treatment: Rest and drink lots of fluids
Get a blood test (CBC / platelet count) early
Daily monitoring by a doctor in the first week
medications: Paracetamol only for fever
AVOID aspirin and ibuprofen — they raise bleeding risk
precautions: Remove stagnant water around the home
diet: Papaya leaf extract is popular but unproven — ask your doctor
diseases.seeDoctor: Bleeding, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or sudden drop in fever with weakness — go to hospital now.
tests: Complete blood count with platelet count

diseases.name: Typhoid Fever
diseases.description: A bacterial infection (Salmonella Typhi) from contaminated food or water, with prolonged fever and stomach upset.
treatment: Blood culture or Widal/typhidot test to confirm
Antibiotics as prescribed — complete the course
Rest and hydration
medications: Prescription antibiotics (e.g. azithromycin, ceftriaxone) chosen by your doctor
diet: Avoid street food and raw salads
diseases.seeDoctor: Fever beyond 3 days, severe belly pain, or confusion needs urgent evaluation.

diseases.name: Hepatitis A
diseases.description: A liver infection from contaminated food or water. It usually clears on its own in weeks.
treatment: Rest and plenty of fluids
Avoid alcohol and unnecessary medicines
Small, light meals if you feel nauseous
medications: No specific antiviral; avoid excess paracetamol and other liver-straining drugs
precautions: Drink safe water; wash hands before eating
diseases.seeDoctor: Persistent vomiting, confusion, bleeding, or yellow eyes that keep worsening.

diseases.name: Hepatitis B
diseases.description: A liver infection spread through blood and body fluids; it can become long-term.
treatment: Specialist monitoring of the liver and virus levels
Antiviral medicines for chronic infection
Avoid alcohol completely
medications: Tenofovir or entecavir for chronic infection: prescription only
precautions: Hepatitis B vaccine, including for newborns
Safe sex; never share needles or razors
diseases.seeDoctor: Yellow eyes, dark urine or abdominal swelling; get tested after any exposure.

diseases.name: Hepatitis C
diseases.description: A blood-borne liver infection that can silently damage the liver; modern medicines can cure it.
treatment: Confirm with an RNA test
Direct-acting antiviral tablets for 8–12 weeks cure over 95% of people
Liver scan to check for scarring
medications: Direct-acting antivirals: prescription only
precautions: Use only sterile injection and tattoo equipment
There is no vaccine; get screened if at risk
diseases.seeDoctor: Yellow eyes, swelling of the abdomen or legs, or confusion.

diseases.name: Hepatitis D
diseases.description: A liver infection that only occurs in people who already have hepatitis B and makes it more severe.
treatment: Specialist care and regular liver monitoring
Antiviral treatment decided by a hepatologist
Avoid alcohol completely
medications: Specialist-directed antiviral therapy only
precautions: Hepatitis B vaccination prevents hepatitis D
diseases.seeDoctor: Yellow eyes, abdominal swelling or confusion. Any hepatitis B patient with new symptoms should be reviewed.

diseases.name: Hepatitis E
diseases.description: A liver infection from contaminated water. It is usually short-lived but can be severe in pregnancy.
treatment: Rest and plenty of fluids
Avoid alcohol and unnecessary medicines
Hospital care if severe or if you are pregnant
medications: No specific antiviral for most people; avoid liver-straining drugs
diseases.seeDoctor: Pregnant women with jaundice need urgent care; also seek help for vomiting that will not stop or confusion.

diseases.name: Alcoholic Hepatitis
diseases.description: Liver inflammation caused by heavy drinking, ranging from mild to life-threatening.
treatment: Stop alcohol completely: this is the most important step
Nutritional support; hospital care for severe cases
Specialist-guided medicines and alcohol-dependence support
medications: Do not self-medicate; many drugs strain the liver
Steroids only in selected severe cases under a specialist
tests: Liver function tests, INR and blood count
precautions: Check every medicine with your doctor
diet: Less salt if you have fluid build-up
diseases.seeDoctor: Yellow eyes, black stools, vomiting blood or confusion: go to hospital immediately.

diseases.name: Tuberculosis (TB)
diseases.description: A bacterial infection mainly of the lungs, spread through the air; it is curable with a full course of treatment.
treatment: Take the full 6-month multi-drug regimen without missing doses
Cover your cough and keep rooms ventilated early on
Screen close contacts
medications: Isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol: prescription only, free through national TB programmes in many countries, including India
diseases.seeDoctor: A cough longer than 2 weeks, blood in sputum, night sweats or weight loss: get tested.

diseases.name: Common Cold
diseases.description: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat that usually clears on its own within a week.
treatment: Rest and drink plenty of warm fluids
Steam inhalation and saline nasal drops
Gargle with warm salt water
medications: Paracetamol for fever or aches
Antihistamine or decongestant for congestion (ask a pharmacist)
diet: Honey with warm water for cough (not for infants)
diseases.seeDoctor: Symptoms last more than 10 days, or you develop high fever or breathing difficulty.
tests: Usually clinical diagnosis — no tests needed
Throat swab only if strep throat is suspected

diseases.name: Pneumonia
diseases.description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs and may fill them with fluid.
treatment: Chest X-ray and clinical evaluation
Antibiotics for bacterial pneumonia
Rest, fluids, and oxygen if needed
medications: Prescription antibiotics or antivirals depending on the cause
Paracetamol for fever
diseases.seeDoctor: Fever with breathlessness or chest pain should be seen the same day.

diseases.name: Hemorrhoids (Piles)
diseases.description: Swollen veins in the rectum or anus that cause pain, itching or bleeding.
treatment: High-fibre diet and plenty of water
Warm sitz baths for 10–15 minutes
Avoid straining and sitting long on the toilet
Procedures are available if symptoms persist
medications: Fibre supplements (psyllium) and stool softeners
Short-term soothing creams
tests: Colonoscopy if bleeding persists or you are over 45
precautions: Stay active and avoid heavy lifting
Respond to the urge to pass stool
diet: At least 2 litres of water a day
diseases.seeDoctor: Heavy or repeated rectal bleeding, black stools or severe pain.

diseases.name: Heart Attack
diseases.description: A blocked blood supply to part of the heart muscle. This is a medical emergency.
treatment: Call your emergency number immediately; do not drive yourself
Sit down, stay calm and loosen tight clothing
Emergency staff may advise chewing aspirin if you are not allergic
Hospital treatment: ECG, clot-dissolving drugs or angioplasty
medications: Aspirin, other antiplatelets, statins and beta-blockers are given by the hospital. Never delay getting care.
precautions: Control blood pressure, cholesterol and sugar
diseases.seeDoctor: EMERGENCY: chest pain or pressure, pain in arm or jaw, sweating or breathlessness. Call emergency services now.

diseases.name: Varicose Veins
diseases.description: Swollen, twisted veins, usually in the legs, caused by weak vein valves.
treatment: Walk daily and raise your legs when resting
Compression stockings
Procedures (laser, radiofrequency, sclerotherapy) for troublesome veins
medications: No medicine cures them; simple pain relief for discomfort
precautions: Avoid standing or sitting for long periods
Avoid tight clothing at the waist and legs
diseases.seeDoctor: Sudden painful swelling or redness (possible clot), skin ulcers, or bleeding.

diseases.name: Hypothyroidism
diseases.description: An underactive thyroid causing tiredness, weight gain, feeling cold and low mood.
treatment: Daily levothyroxine tablet, usually lifelong
Dose guided by TSH blood tests
Take it on an empty stomach, at the same time each day
medications: Levothyroxine: prescription only; keep calcium and iron tablets 4 hours apart
precautions: Recheck TSH 6–8 weeks after any dose change
diet: Adequate iodine and selenium from food
diseases.seeDoctor: Extreme tiredness, confusion, very slow heartbeat or feeling very cold needs emergency review.

diseases.name: Hyperthyroidism
diseases.description: An overactive thyroid causing weight loss, fast heartbeat, sweating and anxiety.
treatment: Anti-thyroid tablets; beta-blockers for symptom control
Radioactive iodine or surgery in selected cases
Regular blood test follow-up
medications: Carbimazole / methimazole and beta-blockers: prescription only
precautions: Do not take iodine or kelp supplements unless advised
diet: Balanced meals with enough calcium and calories
diseases.seeDoctor: Very fast heartbeat with fever or confusion (thyroid storm) is an emergency.

diseases.name: Hypoglycemia (Low Blood Sugar)
diseases.description: Blood sugar that is too low, causing shakiness, sweating, hunger and confusion.
treatment: The "rule of 15": take 15 g fast sugar (glucose tablets or about 150 ml juice)
Re-check after 15 minutes and repeat if still low
Then eat a snack; find out why it happened
medications: Glucagon kits for people on insulin; diabetes medicine doses are adjusted by a doctor
tests: Blood glucose at the time of symptoms
precautions: Do not drink alcohol on an empty stomach
diseases.seeDoctor: Confusion, seizure or fainting is an emergency; also see a doctor for repeated lows.

diseases.name: Osteoarthritis
diseases.description: Wear of joint cartilage, most often in knees, hips and hands, causing pain and stiffness.
treatment: Low-impact exercise and muscle strengthening
Weight loss if overweight
Heat or cold packs; walking aids
Injections or joint replacement for advanced cases
medications: Paracetamol, topical anti-inflammatory gels, short-term tablets with caution
diseases.seeDoctor: Sudden swelling, fever, a locked joint, or pain at night.

diseases.name: Arthritis
diseases.description: Inflammation of one or more joints causing pain, swelling and stiffness.
treatment: Gentle regular exercise and physiotherapy
Warm packs for stiffness, cold packs for swelling
Disease-modifying medicines for inflammatory types (rheumatologist)
medications: Paracetamol or short-term anti-inflammatory tablets (caution for stomach and kidneys)
DMARDs / biologics are prescription only
precautions: Stay active; maintain a healthy weight
diet: Fish, fruit, vegetables and olive oil
diseases.seeDoctor: A hot, swollen joint with fever, morning stiffness over 30 minutes, or joint deformity.

diseases.name: Vertigo (BPPV)
diseases.description: Short spells of spinning dizziness triggered by head movements, caused by tiny crystals displaced in the inner ear.
treatment: A trained clinician or physiotherapist can treat it with the Epley manoeuvre
Sit down at the first sign of spinning
Move your head slowly and sleep with your head slightly raised
medications: Short-term anti-dizziness or anti-nausea tablets only if a doctor advises
precautions: Fall-proof your home (clear floors, good lighting)
Avoid driving or heights while dizzy
diet: Limit alcohol, caffeine and excess salt
diseases.seeDoctor: Vertigo with weakness, double vision, slurred speech or severe headache can be a stroke. Call emergency services.

diseases.name: Acne
diseases.description: Blocked pores and inflammation that cause pimples, blackheads and sometimes cysts.
treatment: Wash gently twice a day; do not squeeze pimples
Use topical treatments consistently for 6–8 weeks
See a dermatologist for moderate to severe or scarring acne
medications: Benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid or adapalene (topical)
Oral antibiotics or isotretinoin: dermatologist only
tests: Hormone tests if periods are irregular
diet: Note and limit your own personal triggers
diseases.seeDoctor: Deep painful cysts, scarring, or no improvement after 6–8 weeks.

diseases.name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
diseases.description: A bacterial infection of the bladder or urinary tract, more common in women.
treatment: Urine test to confirm
Antibiotic course as prescribed
Drink plenty of water
medications: Prescription antibiotics (e.g. nitrofurantoin) chosen after a urine test
diet: Cranberry juice may help prevention but not treatment
diseases.seeDoctor: Fever, back pain or blood in urine suggest a kidney infection — see a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Psoriasis
diseases.description: A long-term skin condition with thick, scaly red patches caused by an overactive immune system.
treatment: Moisturise daily; use prescribed steroid or vitamin-D creams
Light therapy or tablets/injections for moderate to severe disease
Manage stress
medications: Topical steroids and calcipotriol; methotrexate or biologics: specialist only
precautions: Avoid triggers: stress, skin injury, smoking, heavy alcohol
diet: Anti-inflammatory foods: fish, vegetables, olive oil
diseases.seeDoctor: Joint pain or swelling (psoriatic arthritis), widespread redness, or signs of infection.

diseases.name: Impetigo
diseases.description: A contagious bacterial skin infection forming honey-coloured crusts, common in children.
treatment: Gently wash off crusts with soap and water
Antibiotic cream, or tablets if widespread
Keep sores covered; stay home until 48 hours of treatment
medications: Mupirocin or fusidic acid cream; oral antibiotics: prescription only
tests: Swab culture if it keeps returning
precautions: Wash hands often; keep nails short
Clean and cover cuts and insect bites
diseases.seeDoctor: Rapid spread, fever, no improvement after 3 days, or dark urine.
